faq: Which marketplaces should I be on?

It depends on your product. Amazon suits branded, searchable goods, Etsy suits handmade and vintage, eBay suits resale and collectibles, and Walmart is growing. We recommend two or three after reviewing your catalog.
Do I need a seller account on each?
Yes, in your own name. If you do not have them yet, add Account Setup for each new channel. We need the accounts open before we list anything, and we use limited-access users.
How do orders come back to me?
Through a connector app or the marketplace's own tools, depending on your store platform. We choose the option with the best fit and cost, and the monthly app price is paid by you.
Will the same listing work on every marketplace?
Rarely. Each has its own rules for titles, images and categories. We adapt each listing to the channel, and skip products that are not allowed on a particular marketplace.

desc:
Multi-channel selling setup for ecommerce puts the same catalog on more than one marketplace while keeping orders, stock and prices in one place. Ecom Swift LLC connects your store to the marketplaces you choose and maps every product to each channel's rules.

## What is multi-channel selling?

Multi-channel selling means offering your products in several places at once, such as your own online store plus Amazon, eBay, Etsy or Walmart. Each place reaches shoppers who may never visit your website. The cost is more to manage: different category trees, different listing rules and different order screens.

A multi-channel setup connects these places to a single source. Usually that source is your store or a channel management tool.

## Why more channels need a plan

Adding a marketplace without a plan creates scattered work. Products get typed in by hand, titles are copied without checking limits, prices are changed in one place and forgotten in another. Orders arrive in separate inboxes, and stock counts drift.

Not every marketplace suits every product either. A handmade item may fit one channel, while a branded electronics accessory fits another. Choosing the right places first saves effort on channels that will not fit.

## How a good setup affects results

More channels means more places where shoppers can find you, and the setup determines whether you can handle that without errors. When stock moves between channels, you avoid cancelling orders. When prices follow channel rules, you protect margin after fees. When orders flow into one inbox, you ship on time.

We cannot say how many extra sales a channel will bring, since that depends on your products and competition. The setup makes expansion manageable, so growth does not break your fulfillment.

## What a working multi-channel setup includes

- A shortlist of marketplaces that suit your products, with reasons.
- A live connection between your store and each chosen channel.
- Product categories mapped to each channel's category tree.
- Titles and descriptions adjusted to each channel's character limits and style.
- Price rules per channel, allowing for fees and shipping.
- Stock shared across channels from one count.
- Shipping templates for each marketplace.
- Orders from every channel arriving in one place.
- A test order on each channel to check the full path.
- A short guide to running the channels day to day.

## How we set it up

We begin by discussing your catalog, your margins and where you want to sell. We recommend channels, and you decide. Then we connect your store to each marketplace through a suitable integration or the channel's own connector, map categories and set up the title and price rules.

Next we list your products, test the order and stock flow and confirm that updates arrive. The Basic package adds one extra marketplace with a starter selection of products. Standard adds two marketplaces, stock sync and price rules. Premium covers up to three, with channel-specific titles and images, a sales by channel report and a guide for your team. Marketplace and app fees are paid by you directly.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Start with the products that have the best margin after fees.
- Keep one master product sheet and edit it in one place.
- Check each marketplace's category and restricted item rules.
- Test an order on every channel before announcing it.
- Review each channel separately for the first few weeks.

**Avoid:**
- Listing the whole catalog everywhere on day one.
- Using identical prices on channels with very different fees.
- Promising delivery times you cannot meet on every channel.
- Copying text that breaks a channel's content rules.
- Adding channels faster than you can handle the orders.

## Who it is for

A store owner whose own website has plateaued and who wants to reach marketplace shoppers. A seller already on one marketplace who wants a second to reduce dependence on it. A business with a warehouse and a good catalog that wants all channels run from one tidy system.

## What we need from you

Send access as a collaborator or staff user on your store, a product list and your current price and shipping rules. You need a seller account on each marketplace, and we can help you open them as part of a separate service. We never need your passwords. Each marketplace has its own approval steps, and we cannot promise they will accept every product.
